The strongest salon marketing strategy combines both.

*   SEO creates sustainable, long-term traffic.

Together they generate more enquiries while reducing your long-term advertising costs.

Many salon owners begin with Google Ads to generate new business quickly while their SEO gains momentum. As organic rankings improve, they often reduce their advertising spend and continue receiving enquiries through free Google search traffic.

### 🌟 New Series: Google Ads Campaign Structures for Local Businesses 🌟

### I’m excited to launch a new series where I’ll be designing Google Ads campaign structures for small local businesses! This is purely for learning purposes, and I’m open to feedback from experts in the field. If you'd like me to create a structure for your business or have any suggestions, feel free to comment below!

### 🚀 First Example: Salon Business in San Diego 🚀

### A salon wants to promote its manicure and pedicure services with the goal of generating leads through phone calls and website form submissions. Here's how I would approach this campaign:

### Initial Assumptions:

*   The client has a well-optimized Google My Business profile with a good number of reviews and conversion-focused content.
*   The website is simple but effective, and conversion tracking is already in place for both form submissions and phone calls.

### Key Preparations Before Running Ads:

1.  Google My Business Profile: Ensure it’s attractive with images, videos, reviews, and contact information (including phone number).
2.  Conversion Tracking: Properly set up tracking for website form submissions and phone calls.
3.  Link Google Ads & Analytics: Make sure the accounts are linked for accurate performance tracking.
4.  Competitor Research: Analyze pricing and services offered by competitors in the area.
5.  Follow-Up Team: Ensure there is a team ready to follow up on incoming leads.

### Campaign 1: Search Campaign

*   Target Location: 5-15 km radius from the salon's location.
*   Location Setting: Choose "People present in this area" to refine targeting.
*   Budget: $50 - $100 per day.
*   Goal: Set as Leads.
*   Bidding Strategy - Maximise Conversions
*   Network Settings: Untick "Google Search Partners" and "Display Partners."

### Keywords (Broad Match):

*   nail salon near me

*   manicure places near me
*   near nail salon near me

### Headlines (Max 30 characters):

1.  Top-Quality Manicure in San Diego
2.  Luxury Manicure & Pedicure Services
3.  Book Now: San Diego Nail Experts
4.  Affordable Nail Care Near You
5.  5-Star Nail Salon Services

### Descriptions (Max 90 characters):

1.  Pamper yourself with expert manicures. Book your appointment today!
2.  Beautiful nails start here. Call now for top-notch services.
3.  Expert nail care at great prices. Call us for your next manicure!
4.  Manicure & pedicure services designed for you. Visit our salon today!
5.  Nail care with a personal touch. Call for an appointment now!

### Extensions (Assets):

*   Call Assets: Add the salon's phone number and schedule the ads to show during business hours.
*   Sitelink Assets: Example - "Book an Appointment," "View Services," "Our Location," "About Us."
*   Callout Extensions: Example - "Free Parking," "Walk-ins Welcome," "Experienced Staff."
*   Structured Snippet Assets: Example - "Services: Manicure, Pedicure, Nail Art."
*   Image Asset: Include images showcasing your salon.
*   Location Asset: Link the Google My Business profile for easy navigation.

### Campaign 2: Local Listing Ads (Google My Business Profile)

*   Budget: $10 - $25 per day.
*   Location: Target a 5-15 km radius around the salon.
*   Setup: Click the "Advertise" button within Google My Business for easy guidance.
*   Keywords: Use 25 search terms from the list provided above.
*   Schedule: Set the ad to run during business hours to increase call volume.

### Additional Tips:

*   Monitor Performance: Regularly monitor both campaigns and adjust as necessary.
*   Negative Keywords: Use negative keywords to filter out irrelevant searches, as we are using broad match.
*   Expand: In the future, consider adding remarketing campaigns on YouTube and Display for additional visibility.

### [What Barbers, Hairstylists, and Cosmetologists Do](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-2)

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists provide haircutting, hairstyling, and other services related to personal appearance.

### [Work Environment](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-3)

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists work mostly in barbershops or salons. Most are full time, although part-time work is common. Work schedules may vary and often include evenings and weekends.

### [How to Become a Barber, Hairstylist, or Cosmetologist](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-4)

All states require barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists to be licensed. To qualify for a license, candidates typically must graduate from a state-approved barber or cosmetology program and pass an exam.

### [Pay](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-5)

The median hourly wage for barbers was $18.37 in May 2025.

The median hourly wage for hairdressers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists was $17.21 in May 2025.

### [Job Outlook](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-6)

Overall employment of barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists is projected to grow 7 percent from 2025 to 2035, much faster than the average for all occupations.

About 80,300 openings for barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists are projected each year, on average, over the decade. Many of those openings are expected to result from the need to replace workers who transfer to different occupations or exit the labor force, such as to retire.

## What Barbers, Hairstylists, and Cosmetologists Do[About this section](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#TB_inline?height=325&width=325&inlineId=about-what-they-do)

Hairstylists provide hair styling and beauty services.

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists provide haircutting, hairstyling, and other services related to personal appearance.

### Duties

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists typically do the following:

*   Inspect and analyze hair, scalp, and skin to recommend services or treatment
*   Discuss hairstyle options
*   Shampoo, color, lighten, and condition hair
*   Chemically change hair texture
*   Cut, dry, and style hair
*   Trim facial hair
*   Receive payments from client
*   Clean and disinfect all tools and work areas

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists provide hair and other services to enhance clients’ appearance. Common tools may include combs and hairbrushes, clippers and scissors, straight razors, blow dryers, and curling and flat irons. They also may keep records of products used and services provided to clients, such as hair color, hair treatment, and clipper setting.
